supersedes: wave3-independent-1 (protocol.json). Its results in results/first-*.json stay unchanged; nothing in revision 1 is re-scored.
revision_reasons: Revision 1 fixed per-vowel gains by hand; the held-out e gain of 32 clipped two of four candidate predictions, leaving them unscorable for both objectives. Revision 2 sets each vowel's gain by a declared rule from the frozen prediction bank only.
Revision 1 counted candidates as tied only within 1e-12, which is no real margin. Revision 2 declares a tie margin.

Native e/i levels differ by tens of dB between neighbouring anatomies, so held-out error can be mostly level. Revision 2 measures level jumps in the prediction bank before any target exists and reports level separately.
Revision 1 reimplemented coarse scoring. Revision 2 scores both objectives through the production fit_pcm per-trial scorer.
Revision 1 tested ambiguity only with exact duplicates and used one held-out vowel. Revision 2 adds a near-duplicate case and three held-out vowels.

The generating and outside anatomies, source skew and noise seed are new, so no revision-1 target observation is reused. No candidate, objective setting or threshold was chosen from revision-1 held-out scores.
generating_anatomy_rule: 30% of the way from candidate anatomy 0 to candidate anatomy 1; absent from the grid
outside_anatomy_rule: Beyond candidate anatomy 1 by half the grid span in each dimension

gain_rule.basis: Frozen candidate prediction bank only, before any truth or target frame is synthesized
gain_rule.definition: gain(pose) = 10^(peak_target_dbfs/20) / max absolute sample over every candidate's native frame for that pose; the same gain is applied to that pose's predictions and truth frames

level_jump_check.definition: For each pose, RMS level in dB of each candidate's native frame from the frozen bank; flag the pose when the two anatomies at the same source skew differ by more than the threshold. Flagged held-out poses are reported with level differences next to their scores.

tie_rule: A candidate is in the retained set when sqrt(its mean-square discrepancy) is within the margin of the lowest sqrt(mean-square) for that case, objective and stage. Unscorable candidates are never retained.
synthesis_plan: 5 bank members (4 grid candidates and the near duplicate) x 5 vowels = 25; truth for nominal, wrong-fixed-control and outside-support x 5 vowels = 15
scoring: singing_physics.pcm_inverse.score_prediction and candidate_discrepancy, the per-trial scorer inside fit_pcm, for both objectives. Calibration pools both calibration vowels; held-out vowels are scored one at a time.
comparison: Both objectives score the same frozen prediction PCM and the same observation frames. Neither objective receives any additional synthesis.
selection: Rankings use calibration vowels a and i only and are written before any held-out truth frame is synthesized. Every failed, missing and tied candidate is retained.
primary_metrics: hit: for each evaluable (case, held-out vowel) pair, the calibration retained set contains a member of the held-out retained set (scoring only)
regret: lowest held-out sqrt(mean-square) among calibration-retained candidates minus the held-out lowest, within one objective
coverage: scorable candidates per stage, and every failure reason
ambiguity: retained-set sizes, and whether the near duplicate is separated beyond the margin
nearest-grid hit (scoring-only truth): whether the calibration retained set contains the grid candidate nearest the generating anatomy and source
decision_rule: Over the 18 evaluable (case, held-out vowel) pairs: positive for the spectral objective if its hit count exceeds coarse by at least 3 with no more unscorable pairs than coarse; negative if coarse exceeds spectral by at least 3; otherwise inconclusive. The numerical scales of the two objectives differ, so raw discrepancy values are not compared across objectives.
interpretation: Conditional finite-support stress test on synthetic native audio. No anatomical uniqueness, calibrated probability, tissue recovery or human efficacy inference.
